summary: element-plus-vite-cli ships postinstall RAT dropper with hardcoded C2
details: Package is advertised as a Vite CLI for Vue/Element Plus but ships a lib/gradle/... tree containing a base64-encoded payload split across 100+ segments. postinstall-run.cjs reassembles the segments, writes the decoded blob to ~/.gradle/caches/transforms-3/8.7/.../instrumentation-agent-runtime.mjs, and spawns a detached Node process (stdio ignored) to run it. The decoded payload is a full remote-access agent: it POSTs hostname, username, OS type and release to https://npmjs.it.com/api/register (a typosquat of npmjs.com), stores a persistent agent id in ~/.gradle-cache/.aid, and long-polls https://npmjs.it.com/api/task/<uuid> for commands. Supported operations include exec (attacker command string passed to /bin/sh or cmd.exe), ls, download (arbitrary file read, bytes POSTed to /api/file/), upload (attacker bytes written to any path), delete, move, and ps. A C2_TLS_INSECURE env toggle sets NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, and C2_SERVER_URL can override the default C2. Execution is gated on workspace-layout markers (src/api/AITrading.js, src/pages/ETF-quant-trading/history.vue, src/api/cicade.js, src/api/filmRefAudio.ts, src/master/src/router/routes.tsx, update-version.js), so the dropper fires selectively against a specific targeted downstream project. The gradle/instrumentation-agent naming, split-segment base64 encoding, hidden $HOME staging path, detached spawn, and TLS-verify bypass are deliberate concealment inconsistent with the package's declared Vite CLI purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
